issue.description:
Outcome: list consumers can decode one document for every result count while line-oriented streaming stays available explicitly.
Scope: Implement list --json as one JSON array and add --jsonl for the existing object-per-line stream.
Acceptance:
- list --json emits exactly one valid JSON array for zero, one, and many results.
- list --jsonl emits one object per line for nonempty results and no output when empty.
- Plain list output remains usable; focused conformance tests cover all three result counts and both JSON modes.

issue.description:
ADR-005 is Accepted with no implementation bead. Add a `ready_frontier` check under doctor's `dependencies` scope that warns when `open` issues carry an assignee — a state excluded from the ready frontier and permanently unclaimable — printing a bounded sample of offending ids and the exact remedy (`bead update <id> --clear-assignee`). Advisory only: doctor never clears an assignee, not even under `--repair`. Tests: the warning fires for open+assigned issues, stays silent for healthy workspaces and for legitimate `in_progress` claims, and `--repair` provably mutates nothing.

issue.description:
src/service/checkpoint.rs:3567-3568 names the monolithic root objects/{generation_id}.jsonl, derived from the generation ID. Plan section 6.1.1 requires object filenames to contain their content SHA-256 so identical content is reused. The sharded writer already does this (checkpoint.rs:3741-3872); only the monolithic path diverges.

Observed: two consecutive flushes producing byte-identical content created two distinct objects (18 -> 20). Content-addressed reuse can never hit, so every flush leaks a full-workspace-sized immutable object.

Acceptance:
- monolithic root is named from its content SHA-256
- two publications of identical content produce exactly one object, asserted by count in a test
- existing generation-named objects remain readable, or a migration step is specified

Refs: plan 6.1.1, 6.2.1 P1; ADR-003.
issue.title: Content-address the monolithic checkpoint root object
